To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of P, micronutrients, and liming to a low fertility soil increased growth of L. leucocehalia and S. virgate and that dual inoculation with rhizo-bia and mycorrhiza increased growth of all species.
the addition of fertilizers, mycorriza and lime increased growth and nutrient uptake in the leguminous tree seedlings.
The addition of P and N fertilizers, liming, micronutrients, and dual inoculation with rhizo-bial fungi and AMF increased plant growth and nutrient content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of lime and fertilizers on growth of woody leguminous plants in a low fertility tropical soil.
the effect of lime and fertilizers on the growth of selected leguminous trees in low fertility soil.
the use of leguminous trees for the reforestation of degraded areas and the improvement of soil fertility, especially in low fertility soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of fertilizers, liming, mycorrhiza, and rhizobia increased the growth of all the leguminous tree plants, but that the response of the plants varied with the species.
L. leuco-cephala and S. vrigata are the best species for the revegetation and reclamation of degraded lands in the tropics, especially in soils with low fertility.
the dual inoculation of rhizophagy fungi with arbuscular and ericoid mycorrhizae is a good strategy to increase plant growth and development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of mycorrhizae, fertilizers, and liming can improve the growth and yield of woody leguminous trees in low fertility soils, and that dual inoculation with mycobionts and rhizobia is the best strategy.

the dual inoculation with rhizo-bia and arbuscular my-corrhizal fungi (ARMS), liming, and fertilization with P and micronutrients are the most important factors for improving the growth of the leguminous species tested.
the dual inoculation with rhizophila and AMF is a promising strategy for improving the growth and nutrition of woody legume plants in a low fertility tropical soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual inoculation of rhizia and mycorrhiza can increase growth of woody legumes, particularly L. leucocehala and S. Virgata, in low fertility soils.
the dual inoculation of legume species with mycorrhiza and rhizobia is an effective way to improve growth and nutrient uptake in plants grown in a low fertility substrate.
the addition of fertilizers, liming, micronutrients, and inoculation of rhizo and AMF is a good strategy to increase the growth of legume trees in a low fertility substrate.
